- Demo 1, 13x19: background 6, full vertical barrier at c19 color 2. Object color 1 occupied rows 7–11, cols 14–16 (shape rows: c15; c14,c16; c14,c15; c16; c16). - Demo 2, 24x28: background 3, full vertical barrier at c27 color 2. Object color 7 spans rows 4–15, cols 20–23 with missing cells. Output adds color-8 vertical stripe at c22 across all rows, preserving the object. Object centroid column is close to 22 (per-object mean x); this again is a centroid-projection stripe.
- Demo 3, 18x16: background 5, full horizontal barrier at r16 color 2. Object color 1 at rows 5–9, cols 3–5; output adds a full horizontal color-8 stripe at r10. This suggests a more precise rule: cast a line from object's closest edge toward barrier, with line positioned at the first empty row/column immediately after the object's extent on that axis (here r10), rather than centroid. Demo 1 and 2 likewise: first empty column immediately right of object is c17 in demo1 but stripe c15, and c24 in demo2 but stripe c22, so line is not consistently first-empty. Confirmed test: 16x11 background 3, full horizontal barrier r11 color 2, object color 5 at (r14,c6),(r15,c7),(r15,c8), occupied row centroid 14.67.
